newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Electric delays 485 MW nuke start.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Electric delays 485 MW nuke start.

text.p: Wisconsin Electric Power Co said it has delayed the expected restart date of its 485 megawatt (MW) Point Beach nuclear power unit 2, currently down for scheduled maintenance and refueling.
"The proposed restart has been pushed back to March 5," company spokeswoman Jackie Olson said Friday.
The unit had originally been scheduled to resume power production on Feb 14 from a planned outage which began Oct 5, 1996.
"We have a list of startup issues we are discussing with the NRC (Nuclear Regulatory Commission)," Olson said.
Wisconsin Electric has been purchasing power on the spot market to replace that lost by the outage, the spokeswoman said.
The 485 MW Point Beach nuclear power unit 1, also located at Two Rivers, Wis., was operating at its administrative limit of 90 percent of capacity as of early Friday.
Also in Wisconsin, Wisconsin Public Service Corp's 503 MW Kewaunee nuclear power plant located in Carlton, Wis., has been shut since Sept 20 for refueling and maintenance.
Wisconsin Public, a subsidiary of WPS Resources Corp, has said the Kewaunee plant may not restart in the first quarter of 1997 as originally planned due to unexpected steam generator problems.
Wisconsin Electric is a subsidiary of Wisconsin Energy Corp.
